meta.description: Per-instance keyword cluster tags. Each row asserts that a specific span of participant text belongs to a specific cluster from keyword_lexicon.json. The same surface form may appear in different clusters in different segments — context determines the cluster, not the string. Variants in keyword_lexicon.json only rank suggestions in the drawer; they do NOT auto-create rows in this file.
changelog: 1.0 — initial schema. Rows are appended interactively from the segment tag drawer (source: human) or proposed by a future tagging script (source: ai_proposed).

row_shape.keyword_id: Cluster id from keyword_lexicon.json (categories[].keywords[].id). Must exist.
row_shape.segment_id: Segment id from segments.json. Joins to interview/turn/text and absolute char offsets.
row_shape.interview_id: Interview id; redundant with segment_id but kept for filtering convenience.
row_shape.char_start: Absolute char offset of the highlighted span, in the same coordinate system as segments[].char_start (interview-relative).
row_shape.char_end: Absolute char offset, exclusive. surface = transcript.substring(char_start, char_end).
row_shape.surface: Exact substring of the source transcript at [char_start, char_end). Stored verbatim for audit; not used for matching.
row_shape.source: 'human' (added from the drawer) or 'ai_proposed' (added by a future tagger).
row_shape.confidence: Optional. Number in [0,1] for ai_proposed rows; null/omitted for human.
row_shape.review_status: 'confirmed' for human-added rows; 'pending' for ai_proposed rows awaiting review.
row_shape.created_at: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the tag was created.
row_shape.reviewer_notes: Optional free-text note from the reviewer.

notes: A single span MAY belong to more than one cluster — write one row per (cluster, span). Use sparingly; prefer the most specific cluster.
When a cluster is renamed or removed in keyword_lexicon.json, rows here must be migrated or dropped; no cascade is automatic.
Validators (TBD) should ensure: surface == transcript.substring(char_start, char_end), span is fully inside the named segment, keyword_id exists in the lexicon, and no two rows share the natural key.
